The most notable new feature is called the panel - it lets the agent chat open and then sit next to pages from Datasette, for example a table or query page. When combined with datasette-apps this means you can prompt a database-backed app into existence and then modify it from the chat that sits next to that app. You can try it by signing in with your GitHub account to agent.datasette.io. articles.title: Hardening GitHub Actions Against Outside Threats
articles.description: The supply chain attacks that defined 2025 and 2026 did not arrive as typosquats or as newly published malicious packages. They arrived inside legitimate, widely installed packages whose maintainers wrote no malicious code. The malicious code entered during the release, and in most cases the release ran on GitHub Actions. articles.title: I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere) - YouTube
articles.description: I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere) - YouTube Genius piece of OSINT by Colsto, who demonstrates how you can take almost imperceptible background noise of planes from a video soundtrack, figure out their Doppler curves, then cross reference them against ADS-B data to find the exact location of the video based on their speed, distance, and gaps between different flights. Via Lobste.rs Tags: privacy, youtube

articles.title: Composer 2.11 Adds Dependency Cooldowns
articles.description: Composer 2.11 has introduced dependency cooldowns, giving PHP developers a native way to delay newly published package versions before they become eligible for installation. The release arrives nearly a year after developers first requested the feature, bringing Composer into line with package managers that have already adopted minimum release age policies to reduce exposure to supply chain attacks. The new config.policy.cooldown setting allows developers to specify a waiting period in hours,…

articles.description: All PHP projects have one thing in common, regardless of whether they are built on a full-stack framework, on a microservice framework with carefully selected standalone libraries, or as an extension for a CMS: the PHP standard library. Functions such as str_replace() or array_map() and classes like DateTimeImmutable or Uri\Rfc3986\Uri from PHP 8.5 are always available, always work the same, and always have the same meaning.
